This supplies inspectable evidence for [review 5847953578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158848#issuecomment-5847953578). The [Testbox Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36237226704) is canceled, and the review could not inspect its logs; it is not a green CI result. The evidence below comes from retained payload receipts and traces, not from that run’s conclusion.

**Source binding.** This proof applies only to reviewed commit `17514fe6217fcd1a7d0fcdbc6ca7babc37b158e6`, tree `6629da61d733c2afc71d760b73ade796bcab6cf9`. The source capsule used carrier commit `196265bbf60f95b8eb01b5a8f80d4472c2043744` with that same tree; `GIT_COMMIT` bound build metadata to the reviewed commit. Build ID: `2026.9.6-17514fe6217f-2026-09-26T11-00-17.187Z`. This is retained proof, not a rerun of later source compositions or the subsequent signal fix.

| Retained artifact | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Published npm 2026.9.4 tarball | `4f1f656770461d4677dea755b1899cba12b912b06798c89a59e2f0c18688b761` |
| Candidate tarball (98,061,481 bytes) | `a62182d6a3493656a31cee47950b43ea7f0bfae1661d0a2ec55284837b67d82d` |
| Candidate build info | `4f7460fe9e378e1dea2d7368a86538726f2e0da530d2ad13bb5352f9efac2920` |
| Full dist manifest | `08e0f3797e1054e3182d5c42ae541a7d9078739149c77ccf9fb8cce6802e36a9` |
| Evidence archive (168,822,516 bytes) | `39e1d65150802f361569911b95df663af10100bdff9f4ce0c11061389a38ddeb` |

The baseline receipt identifies [the published npm tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw/-/openclaw-2026.9.4.tgz), version `2026.9.4`, with integrity `sha512-lTQpEEe1Xm3u2PCHaPEr+vP8paGk1vLdHuzdItsNToaLI6hAqRVvgJYg+GxukJhETJp4tPy/S1Gftl4KuB8n7A==`. Candidate and installed package manifests contain the same 11,136 file records, including hashes and sizes.

**Command-level receipts.** Paths below are normalized: `<source>` is the frozen checkout, `<proof>` the task-owned harness, and `<evidence>` the isolated output directory. These are parsed receipt fields, not a new execution recipe.

```text
source: remote-receipt.json; status=passed
node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --source-dir <source> --output-dir <evidence>/package --output-name candidate.tgz
  exit=0; seconds=512.903
python3 <proof>/launcher/run-built-capture-launcher-proof.py [recorded source/build identity assertions; Node 24.19.0; Bun 1.4.2]
  exit=0; seconds=9.012
node <proof>/run-subprocess.mjs <source> 17514fe6217fcd1a7d0fcdbc6ca7babc37b158e6 <evidence>/subprocess
  exit=0; seconds=4.788
node <proof>/prepare-upgrade-adapter.mjs <source> <evidence>/adapter
  exit=0; seconds=0.021
/bin/bash <evidence>/adapter/run-upgrade-capture.sh
  exit=0; seconds=66.005
  maintained update_candidate dispatch: openclaw update --tag file:<evidence>/package/candidate.tgz --yes --json --no-restart
```

The adapter retained the maintained upgrade-survivor function prefix, including `update_candidate`, success classification, immutable baseline verification, and candidate/installed comparison. Its phase list was narrowed for this capture-cleanup cell. Recorded maintained-prefix SHA-256: `ce7ea0db84175e4323b0554230121592e3c697e514cae02e8664a663933ab7de`.

**Actual published-driver lineage and cleanup.** The independent published-source record locates `continueMigratedUpdateInFreshProcess` in `dist/update-command-migrated-GnpzJmQa.mjs:76` (file SHA-256 `585a7bb1cc1c9cd4a685a4944863d98d924d72e5b389ba3b3727b1b110e377fd`). It builds the candidate worker command from `runtimeProcessEntrypoints.updateMigratedFinalize.distWorkerPath` and passes the real finalization input on stdin. Runtime records then show:

```json
{
  "publishedProcess": {"role":"update","packageVersion":"2026.9.4","pid":10060,"parentPid":10053,"exitCode":0},
  "candidateWorker": {"pid":10837,"parentPid":10060,"argv":["<installed>/dist/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.js"],"commit":"17514fe6217fcd1a7d0fcdbc6ca7babc37b158e6","mode":"none"},
  "trace": [
    {"index":6,"event":"capture-writes-submitted","sessionId":"update-capture-proof-10837"},
    {"index":7,"event":"capture-writes-observed","sessionId":"update-capture-proof-10837","blobId":"97dd3df807ff010e11f48144"},
    {"index":8,"event":"capture-drained"},
    {"index":9,"event":"state-close-start","drained":true},
    {"index":10,"event":"state-close-end","drained":true},
    {"index":11,"event":"worker-exit","code":0}
  ],
  "cleanupSummary": {"status":"passed","doctor":[],"checks":[],"finalizationCount":1},
  "updateJson": {"status":"ok","mode":"npm","beforeVersion":"2026.9.4","afterVersion":"2026.9.6"},
  "successfulUpdateCheck": {"availability":"captured","outcome":"passed"},
  "upgradeSummary": {"status":"passed","candidateInstallMode":"updater","updateRestartMode":"manual","updateOutcome":"success","failure":null}
}
```

The worker invocation has neither `--check` nor `--doctor`. A task-local preload registered a synthetic capture callback with the real cleanup owner; it used the actual async store to write/read the session, event and blob, end the session, release the worker lease, and settle asynchronously. It delegated state close and error formatting to their real implementations. The published cell used no injected cleanup faults, and its preload was inert during capability checks. Post-exit SQLite assertions confirmed `ended_at=3`, one event with `flow_id=pending-at-finalization`, and the recorded blob ID. No successful result or update-ledger state was injected. Raw finalizer trace SHA-256: `16484a8de649b4581caeea7f9c21983bda9ca413ffe53323a238794b48e932f9`.

The separate subprocess matrix deliberately covered failure reporting as well:

| Cell | Worker PID | Expected/observed exit | Capture drain / state-close start / end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Successful capability check | 9516 | 0 / 0 | 8 / 9 / 10 |
| Primary rejection | 9529 | 1 / 1 | 8 / 9 / 10 |
| Cleanup failures after real cleanup | 9602 | 1 / 1 | 8 / 9 / 10 |
| Primary rejection plus cleanup failures | 9624 | 1 / 1 | 8 / 9 / 10 |

All four persisted the synthetic session/event. In the combined case, the reported `AggregateError` retained the primary rejection as `cause` and first member, then the capture cleanup aggregate and state cleanup error. The latter errors were exactly `synthetic-capture-cleanup-failure` and `synthetic-state-cleanup-failure`; fault injection occurred after real cleanup.

The built-launcher receipt additionally records successful Node 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.2 runs of `proxy run`, `proxy sessions`, `proxy query`, and capture-enabled normal CLI initialization/finalization. Both runtimes persisted the synthetic loopback request/response bytes and ended their sessions. Observed synchronous gzip/gunzip counts were zero. Node `proxy run` had zero observed main-thread SQLite calls; sessions/query had other CLI SQLite activity. Bun SQLite was deliberately uninstrumented.

**Payload result versus lease cleanup.** Retained dispatch timing and stop receipts are distinct:

```json
{
  "dispatchReceipt": {"exit":0},
  "wrapperTiming": {"commandMs":668248,"totalMs":668713,"exitCode":0,"runStatus":"succeeded"},
  "evidenceVerification": {"status":"passed","verifiedFiles":154,"nestedTarballs":"Verified in archive; not duplicated on disk"},
  "subsequentLeaseStop": {"exitCode":0,"reportedState":"stopped (completed)"}
}
```

The stop log explicitly notes that delegated Testbox Actions runs can appear canceled during external lease cleanup. These receipts establish payload success and a later successful stop; they do not independently prove why GitHub assigned its canceled conclusion. The full raw archive is retained locally, not attached here; the excerpts and hashes above are operator-provided evidence, not publicly downloadable or independently authenticated CI artifacts.

Two initial dispatch attempts failed before remote sync/command because explicit environment forwarding was unsupported. The successful build emitted a nonterminal `context canceled` line but exited 0. After successful payload completion, portal sync emitted `context deadline exceeded`. `update-result-check.log` contains an `ok != warning` assertion because the unchanged harness first tries the recoverable-warning classifier; its subsequent success classifier passed, as recorded above. A slow per-file download was stopped; the compact export then verified all 154 retained files. Dependencies and disposable caches were excluded.

Scope remains synthetic loopback and isolated update/finalizer proof. This does not prove a live-provider session, real-operator update, restart continuity (`--no-restart` was used), Bun SQLite threading, or zero SQL across the whole CLI. No pre-fix negative control or newer-source rerun was performed.

@clawsweeper re-review

The signal-exit finding is fixed in 441e8a918f66: active capture joins the existing signal barrier before worker-source finalization. Both managed CLI signal cases and actual OS SIGINT/SIGTERM cases failed before repair and pass afterward; 277 focused tests, types, lint, import cycles, line-cap, and source inventory pass. Independent review is clean through P2. The PR body now links inspectable published-driver receipts with explicit source binding and the canceled Actions-run limitation.
